quests.instruction: Build the body paragraph starting from its topic sentence.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that team sports teach cooperation
options: Team sports teach cooperation in ways that individual activities rarely do.
That willingness to set personal instinct aside is cooperation in its most practical form.
A player has to adjust their own instincts to fit a plan shared by the whole team.
A striker who could easily shoot instead passes to a better-placed teammate because the team's success matters more than personal credit.
quests.hint: Start with the sentence naming this paragraph's one idea, then look for the general point, a specific case of it, and the sentence tying it back.
quests.explanation: The topic sentence tells the reader what this paragraph is about. The supporting point explains the mechanism in general terms, and the example shows that mechanism in a specific moment, which is why it follows rather than leads. The link back closes by naming what the example actually demonstrates.
quests.thesisStatement: Team sports teach cooperation by requiring players to set personal instinct aside for the group's benefit.

quests.instruction: Assemble this paragraph so its claim, reasoning, evidence, and closing connection appear in the right order.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph explaining why written checklists reduce mistakes at work
options: A written checklist reduces mistakes that memory alone tends to miss.
Hospitals that introduced a short pre-surgery checklist saw measurable drops in preventable errors within the first year.
Under time pressure, people skip steps they know perfectly well, simply because attention narrows to whatever feels most urgent.
A simple list, in other words, protects against the very moments when memory is least reliable.
quests.hint: The explanation should describe a general human tendency before the evidence shows that tendency being addressed in a real setting.
quests.explanation: The topic sentence states the paragraph's claim. The explanation describes why memory fails under pressure, which prepares the reader to understand why the hospital evidence matters. The link back interprets that evidence in terms of the original claim, closing the paragraph.
quests.thesisStatement: A written checklist reduces mistakes that memory alone tends to miss under pressure.

quests.instruction: Order this body paragraph so the example illustrates a point that has already been explained.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that asking for feedback early improves a piece of writing
options: A writer who shares a messy outline before drafting can restructure in minutes what might otherwise take days to unpick from finished paragraphs.
Early feedback, then, protects a writer's time as much as it improves the final piece.
A reader can catch a structural problem in a rough draft before a writer has spent hours polishing sentences that may not survive a rewrite.
Asking for feedback early in the writing process saves more revision time than asking for it at the end.
quests.hint: Find the sentence that explains why timing matters in general, then the one that shows that general point happening to a specific writer.
quests.explanation: The topic sentence states the timing claim. The supporting point explains why early feedback saves time, in general terms, and the example shows one writer experiencing that exact benefit. The link back restates the value once the example has demonstrated it.
quests.thesisStatement: Asking for feedback early in the writing process saves more revision time than asking for it at the end.

quests.instruction: This paragraph presents evidence before explaining it. Reorder so the reasoning comes first.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that regular practice matters more than natural talent in learning an instrument
options: Talent may explain who starts ahead, but practice explains who ends up ahead.
Consistent practice shapes a musician's skill more than natural talent does.
Skill in playing an instrument depends on physical patterns built through repetition, something talent alone cannot shortcut.
Students who practised thirty minutes daily for a year consistently outperformed students who practised only before lessons, regardless of how naturally gifted either group seemed at the start.
quests.hint: Decide whether the paragraph should explain the mechanism before or after showing the study result, and place the interpretation accordingly.
quests.explanation: The claim states the position. The reasoning explains the mechanism, repetition building physical patterns, which prepares the reader to interpret the evidence correctly once it appears. The interpretation closes by drawing the contrast the claim promised.
quests.thesisStatement: Consistent practice shapes a musician's skill more than natural talent does.

quests.instruction: Arrange this paragraph so the evidence appears only after the reader knows what claim it is meant to prove.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that eating breakfast improves concentration in morning classes
options: Students given a simple breakfast before a maths test scored noticeably higher than students who skipped it, even when both groups had studied equally.
Eating breakfast improves how well students concentrate during morning lessons.
The extra energy, not extra knowledge, appears to be what made the difference.
A body that has gone without food overnight relies on stored energy that starts running low well before lunchtime.
quests.hint: The mechanism should be understood before the test result can be interpreted correctly, so place it accordingly.
quests.explanation: The claim states the position on breakfast and concentration. The mechanism explains why energy runs low without it, which the evidence then demonstrates through a comparison. The interpretation closes by naming what the evidence actually shows, energy rather than knowledge.
quests.thesisStatement: Eating breakfast improves how well students concentrate during morning lessons.

quests.instruction: Order this paragraph so a statistic is placed where it supports rather than replaces the reasoning.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that shorter commutes improve employee wellbeing
options: A shorter daily commute does more for an employee's wellbeing than most workplace perks.
Employees with commutes under twenty minutes reported noticeably lower stress levels than those commuting over an hour, even when job satisfaction was otherwise similar.
Time spent commuting is time taken directly from sleep, exercise, or unwinding, with no way to recover it later in the day.
The commute itself, not the job, appears to be driving that difference in stress.
quests.hint: A statistic works best once the reader understands why the pattern it describes would make sense. Place the reasoning before the number.
quests.explanation: The claim states the position. The reasoning explains why commuting time specifically damages wellbeing, which prepares the reader to interpret the statistic that follows. The interpretation draws the conclusion the statistic supports, closing the paragraph.
quests.thesisStatement: A shorter daily commute does more for an employee's wellbeing than most workplace perks.

quests.instruction: Every sentence here belongs, but one is tempting to misplace. Restore paragraph unity by ordering correctly.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that public speaking courses should be part of secondary education
options: Public speaking deserves a formal place in the secondary school curriculum.
Some students discover through a speaking course that clear thinking and clear speaking depend on each other far more than they expected.
Teaching this skill early gives every student a tool they will use long after school ends.
Very few adult jobs avoid the need to explain an idea clearly to a room of people, whether colleagues or customers.
quests.hint: The tempting detail could wander toward general classroom benefits. Check that it stays tied specifically to public speaking's value.
quests.explanation: The topic sentence states the paragraph's claim. The supporting reason gives the general workplace justification, and the tempting detail, about thinking and speaking together, stays anchored to public speaking specifically rather than drifting into a separate point about classrooms generally. The link back closes the paragraph.
quests.thesisStatement: Public speaking deserves a formal place in the secondary school curriculum because nearly every career eventually requires it.

quests.instruction: One sentence could easily pull this paragraph toward a different subject. Keep it anchored and order the paragraph.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that community sports leagues benefit adults, not just children
options: A league built for children, then, quietly does just as much for the parents standing on the sideline.
For many working adults, a weekly match is one of the few remaining commitments that gets them moving regularly.
Community sports leagues offer real benefits to adults, not only to the children most leagues are built around.
The friendships formed on a five-a-side team often outlast the season itself, becoming part of an adult's wider social life.
quests.hint: The detail about friendships could tempt a writer into a separate essay about adult loneliness. Keep it tied to sports leagues specifically.
quests.explanation: The topic sentence states the claim about adult benefit. The supporting reason addresses physical activity, and the anchored detail extends the benefit to friendship without drifting into a broader essay about loneliness. The link back closes by tying both benefits to the original claim.
quests.thesisStatement: Community sports leagues benefit adults through regular activity and lasting friendships, not just the children they are built for.

quests.instruction: This paragraph risks splitting into two topics. Order it so unity is preserved around one central claim.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that reading fiction builds empathy
options: Fiction, in this way, rehearses empathy before real life asks for it.
Reading fiction builds empathy in a way that few other habits do as reliably.
A reader who spends a novel inside a character coping with grief often recognises that same grief more clearly in a friend months later.
A novel places a reader inside another person's thoughts for hours at a time, something even a close friendship rarely offers so directly.
quests.hint: The example could tempt a writer toward a general point about grief. Keep it tied specifically to fiction's role in building empathy.
quests.explanation: The topic sentence states the claim. The supporting reason explains the mechanism, sustained access to another mind, and the anchored example shows that mechanism producing empathy later in life, staying tied to fiction rather than becoming a separate point about grief itself. The link back closes the paragraph.
quests.thesisStatement: Reading fiction builds empathy by giving readers sustained access to another person's inner life.

quests.instruction: Order this comparison-based body paragraph so the two ideas are contrasted clearly before the judgment.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph comparing renting and buying a first home
options: For someone still unsure where they will be living in five years, that flexibility usually outweighs the equity.
Buying builds equity instead of paying toward someone else's mortgage, but ties a person to one place for years.
Renting and buying a first home suit different situations more than either one suits everybody.
Renting keeps a person flexible, free to move for a job or a relationship without selling anything first.
quests.hint: A comparison paragraph should present both sides fairly before making a judgment that depends on both having been stated.
quests.explanation: The topic sentence frames the comparison. Both sides are presented in turn, renting's flexibility and buying's equity and commitment, and the judgment weighs them against each other, which requires both to already be on the table.
quests.thesisStatement: Renting and buying a first home suit different situations, and flexibility often matters more for someone uncertain about the future.

quests.instruction: Arrange this compare/contrast paragraph so the shared ground comes first and the distinguishing point comes after both subjects are introduced.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph comparing studying alone and studying in a group
options: Studying alone lets a student move at their own pace, spending extra time only where they personally struggle.
Both studying alone and studying in a group can help a student prepare for an exam.
The real difference is not effectiveness but honesty: a group is harder to fool about what you actually know.
Studying in a group exposes gaps a student did not know they had, since explaining an idea to someone else reveals what is not yet understood.
quests.hint: The shared ground should come before either subject is detailed, and the distinguishing point should draw on both details rather than introduce a new idea.
quests.explanation: The shared ground establishes what both methods have in common. Each subject is then detailed in turn, and the distinguishing point closes by contrasting them directly, which only works once both details have been given.
quests.thesisStatement: Studying in a group is often more honest about revealing what a student does not yet understand.

quests.instruction: This paragraph compares two options but risks judging before both are described. Correct the order.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph comparing email and instant messaging for workplace communication
options: Instant messaging suits quick questions where waiting for a reply would slow work down for no good reason.
Using the wrong one for the wrong purpose, more than either tool itself, is what usually causes workplace communication to feel chaotic.
Email suits messages that need a record, time to think through, or more than one recipient reading carefully.
Email and instant messaging serve different purposes at work, even though both often get used for everything.
quests.hint: Each option should be described on its own terms before the judgment compares the pattern of appropriate and inappropriate use.
quests.explanation: The topic sentence frames the comparison. Each option is described for what it does well, and the judgment closes by identifying the real source of communication problems, a point that depends on both descriptions already being clear.
quests.thesisStatement: Email and instant messaging each suit different purposes, and using the wrong one for a task is what usually causes confusion.

quests.instruction: Order this problem-solution paragraph so the benefit follows a solution that follows a clearly stated problem.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph proposing a fix for long queues at a school cafeteria
options: Students would gain several extra minutes to actually eat and rest before their next lesson.
Pre-paid meal cards linked to a chosen weekly menu would let most students walk straight to their food.
Much of the delay comes from every student paying individually at the till, even for the same few meal combinations.
Lunch queues at the cafeteria regularly eat into the twenty-five minutes students have to eat.
quests.hint: A solution should answer a specific named cause, not the problem in general. Place the cause before the solution that targets it.
quests.explanation: The problem states what is wrong. The cause narrows the reason behind it, which the solution then directly addresses. The benefit closes the paragraph by describing what students gain, which depends on the solution already being proposed.
quests.thesisStatement: Pre-paid meal cards would fix long cafeteria queues by removing the slowest part of the current payment process.

quests.instruction: Arrange this paragraph so the solution responds to the specific cause rather than the general problem.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph proposing a fix for low attendance at a company's optional training sessions
options: Optional training sessions at the company are rarely attended by more than a handful of employees.
Most sessions are scheduled during the busiest hours of the day, competing directly with employees' regular workload.
Moving sessions to the final hour before employees usually leave would remove that direct competition for time.
Attendance would likely rise simply because employees would no longer have to choose between training and their actual job.
quests.hint: The solution should target the timing cause specifically, not attendance in general. Place the cause before the fix aimed at it.
quests.explanation: The problem states the low attendance. The cause identifies scheduling as the specific reason, which the solution answers directly by proposing a different time. The benefit closes by explaining why that particular fix should work.
quests.thesisStatement: Moving training sessions to a less competitive time slot would likely raise attendance significantly.

quests.instruction: This paragraph proposes a solution before naming its cause. Reorder it so the fix responds to something the reader already understands.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph proposing a fix for frequent miscommunication between two departments in a company
options: Marketing and product teams at the company regularly plan campaigns around features that get delayed or cut.
The two teams currently work from separate planning documents that are rarely compared until a launch date is close.
Campaigns would then be built around features that actually exist by the time they need to launch.
A single shared timeline, updated by both teams, would let each side see changes as soon as they happen.
quests.hint: The solution addresses a specific cause: separate documents. That cause has to be named before the shared timeline can be understood as a direct answer to it.
quests.explanation: The problem introduces the recurring conflict. The cause explains the structural reason it keeps happening, separate documents, which the solution answers directly. The benefit closes by describing the practical result of fixing that specific cause.
quests.thesisStatement: A single shared planning timeline would fix the miscommunication between marketing and product teams.

quests.instruction: This paragraph currently reads like a list. Reorder it so the explanation actually develops the claim.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph explaining why active recall is more effective than rereading notes
options: Actively trying to recall the idea without looking exposes exactly what has and has not actually been learned.
Testing yourself on material works better than simply rereading it.
Rereading feels productive because the words become familiar with each pass.
That familiarity, though, is often mistaken for understanding, since recognising an idea is easier than producing it from memory.
quests.hint: Development means each sentence should deepen the one before it, not just add another fact. Find the sentence that explains why the alternative fails before the better approach appears.
quests.explanation: The claim states the position. Naming the weak alternative gives the reader something familiar to compare against, and the explanation of its shortfall deepens that comparison before the stronger approach is offered as the answer to the very problem just described.
quests.thesisStatement: Testing yourself on material through active recall works better than simply rereading it.

quests.instruction: Turn this list-like set of sentences into a developed paragraph by ordering it correctly.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph explaining why slow, deliberate practice beats simply repeating a skill many times
options: Repetition alone often just reinforces whatever habits, good or bad, a person already has.
Many people assume that doing something over and over will naturally make them better at it.
Deliberate, focused practice improves a skill faster than simply repeating it many times.
Focusing closely on the specific part that keeps going wrong corrects those habits instead of repeating them.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that names a common but flawed belief, the one that explains exactly why it is flawed, and the one that answers that flaw.
quests.explanation: The claim opens with the position. The common assumption states what most people believe, which the following sentence complicates by explaining why repetition alone fails. The better approach closes by directly answering that failure.
quests.thesisStatement: Deliberate, focused practice improves a skill faster than simply repeating it many times.

quests.instruction: Order this paragraph so each sentence builds on the reasoning of the one before it, rather than sitting beside it as a separate point.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph explaining why constructive criticism helps more than praise alone
options: Clear, specific criticism removes the guesswork by pointing directly at what needs to change.
Constructive criticism helps someone improve more than praise alone ever could.
Without that specific information, improvement becomes a matter of guessing rather than adjusting.
Praise feels good, but it rarely tells a person exactly what to keep doing or change next time.
quests.hint: Each sentence should explain the gap left by the one before it. Find where the paragraph identifies the actual problem with praise before offering the fix.
quests.explanation: The claim states the position on criticism. The limitation of praise names its shortfall, which the deeper reason explains further by describing what that shortfall causes, guesswork. The final sentence answers that exact guesswork with what criticism specifically provides.
quests.thesisStatement: Constructive criticism helps someone improve more reliably than praise alone.

quests.instruction: This paragraph serves one clear purpose within a larger essay. Order it so each sentence plays its distinct role.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph that provides the strongest counterexample against banning phones in classrooms entirely
options: A blanket ban forces these students to either break the rule or risk their own health.
A ban with a clear medical exception would address distraction without creating that impossible choice.
Many schools have banned phones from classrooms entirely to reduce distraction.
Some students, though, rely on a phone app to manage medical conditions such as diabetes, checking readings discreetly during lessons.
quests.hint: This paragraph's job is to complicate a rule with a real exception, then propose a narrow fix. Order it so the exception is understood before the fix is proposed.
quests.explanation: The acknowledged rule states the policy being examined. The counterexample introduces the specific case that complicates it, and its consequence explains why that case matters enough to address. The limited concession closes by proposing a narrow fix rather than reversing the whole rule.
quests.thesisStatement: A blanket phone ban should include a clear medical exception rather than applying without exception.

quests.instruction: This paragraph's job is to introduce a counterargument the essay will later answer. Order it so the counterargument reads as genuinely persuasive before it is limited.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph presenting the strongest case against remote work becoming permanent for most office roles
options: New employees, in particular, often struggle to learn unwritten workplace norms without being physically present to observe them.
A junior employee working from home may go months without noticing habits, shortcuts, or warning signs that a colleague would absorb naturally in an office.
Not every argument favours remote work becoming the permanent default.
This gap matters most in the first year of a job, less so once someone is established.
quests.hint: A fair counterargument paragraph should state the case strongly, support it, and only then note its limits, rather than undermining it too early.
quests.explanation: The setup signals the paragraph's purpose. The strongest counterpoint states the case directly, and the support gives it real weight before the limiting note narrows its scope, which would weaken the argument if placed any earlier.
quests.thesisStatement: Remote work poses a genuine challenge for new employees still learning a workplace's unwritten norms.

quests.instruction: This paragraph exists to test a claim against an exception. Order it so the exception is treated fairly before the claim is refined.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph examining an exception to the claim that specialising early leads to greater career success
options: A narrow skill set built around one tool or method leaves less room to adapt when that tool falls out of use.
In fast-changing fields such as technology, however, early specialists sometimes find their specific skill outdated within a few years.
Early specialising pays off best in stable fields, while adaptable generalist skills matter more where change is constant.
Specialising early in a career often leads to faster advancement than staying generalist.
quests.hint: The exception should be explained thoroughly enough that the refined claim reads as an honest conclusion, not a contradiction.
quests.explanation: The general claim states the common pattern. The exception complicates it with a specific case, and the explanation clarifies why that case breaks the pattern. The refined claim closes by integrating both the rule and its exception into one balanced position.
quests.thesisStatement: Early specialising pays off best in stable fields, while adaptable generalist skills matter more where change is constant.

quests.instruction: Order this paragraph so its natural transition word reflects a genuine logical relationship, not a positional trick.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph explaining why a company's return policy affects customer trust
options: Customers are more willing to try an unfamiliar product when they know a mistake will not cost them anything.
Trust, in the end, grows less from the product itself than from how safe a customer feels trying it.
A generous return policy builds customer trust in ways that price alone cannot.
A strict policy, however, can make customers hesitate even over products they would probably like, simply because the risk feels too high.
quests.hint: The word 'however' should mark a genuine contrast in the argument, not just sit in a random position. Check which sentence it actually belongs after.
quests.explanation: The claim states the position. The first reason explains the mechanism through a generous case, and the contrasting reason uses 'however' to genuinely oppose that mechanism through a strict case, which is why it must follow rather than open the paragraph. The synthesis closes by drawing a conclusion from both.
quests.thesisStatement: A generous return policy builds customer trust more effectively than price alone.

quests.instruction: This paragraph uses 'therefore' to mark a real conclusion, not a guessable final position. Order it correctly.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph explaining why unclear instructions slow down a team project
options: Team projects frequently stall in their first week for reasons that have nothing to do with the work itself.
Clear, written instructions are therefore not a formality but a genuine safeguard against wasted effort.
Team members end up working from conflicting versions of the same task, discovering the mismatch only once work has already started.
Instructions handed out verbally, without anything written down, get remembered differently by different people.
quests.hint: Check that 'therefore' follows a real chain of cause and consequence rather than simply appearing at the end because conclusions usually go last.
quests.explanation: The observation raises the pattern needing explanation. The cause and consequence build the chain that the word 'therefore' then genuinely concludes from, connecting the safeguard directly to the specific problem just described rather than to a vague general idea.
quests.thesisStatement: Clear, written instructions are a genuine safeguard against wasted effort in team projects.

quests.instruction: Order this paragraph so 'similarly' connects two examples that actually share the same underlying point.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph explaining why small, visible progress keeps people motivated
options: In both cases, the nearby, visible marker does more to sustain effort than the far-off outcome ever could.
A runner training for a race often sticks with it longer when an app shows weekly distance slowly increasing.
Similarly, a language learner is more likely to continue when an app shows a streak of daily practice rather than a far-off fluency goal.
Visible signs of progress keep people motivated more reliably than a distant final goal.
quests.hint: The word 'similarly' should introduce a second example that genuinely parallels the first, not just any related fact.
quests.explanation: The claim states the position. The first example shows the pattern in one context, and 'similarly' introduces a second example that shares the same underlying mechanism, which is why it must follow rather than open the paragraph. The conclusion draws the shared point from both.
quests.thesisStatement: Visible, nearby signs of progress keep people motivated more reliably than a distant final goal.

quests.instruction: Two orders might look plausible at first glance. Determine which one actually preserves the argument's logic.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that peer review improves the quality of published research
options: Independent reviewers catch errors and gaps in reasoning that a single research team, close to its own work, can easily miss.
Reviewers can also be slow, inconsistent, or occasionally biased toward familiar approaches over new ones.
The process is therefore worth keeping, not because it is flawless, but because the alternative, no independent check at all, is worse.
Peer review improves the overall quality of published research, even though the process is far from perfect.
quests.hint: Placing the limitation before the mechanism would confuse the reader about what is even being limited. Establish the benefit first.
quests.explanation: The claim states a qualified position from the start. The mechanism explains why peer review helps, which must be understood before the limitation can meaningfully qualify it. The refined position closes by weighing the benefit against the flaw already described.
quests.thesisStatement: Peer review improves the overall quality of published research, even though the process itself is imperfect.

quests.instruction: This paragraph could be ordered two ways; only one keeps the counterpoint from undermining the claim too early. Choose it.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that open-book exams still test understanding effectively
options: Open-book exams can test genuine understanding just as effectively as closed-book ones.
Critics argue that having access to notes makes the exam too easy to pass without real knowledge.
The presence of a textbook, then, changes what is being tested rather than lowering the standard.
In practice, open-book questions are usually designed to require applying information, not locating it, which notes alone cannot answer.
quests.hint: If the objection appeared before the claim, the reader would not yet know what position is being defended. Establish the claim first.
quests.explanation: The claim states the position clearly before any challenge appears. The objection is then anticipated fairly, and the response answers it directly, which must follow the objection to make sense. The reinforced position closes by restating the claim in light of the answered objection.
quests.thesisStatement: Open-book exams can test genuine understanding just as effectively as closed-book ones.

quests.instruction: Only one order avoids asking the reader to accept a conclusion before its full reasoning has appeared. Find it.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that a four-day work week can maintain productivity
options: A four-day work week can maintain the same productivity as a five-day one.
In trials, total output stayed roughly the same, suggesting that the missing day was mostly filled with tasks that did not need to exist.
Some managers worry that fewer hours simply means less work gets done overall.
Employees given one fewer day often compress low-value tasks and meetings that previously stretched to fill the time available.
quests.hint: The doubt should be answered with the evidence, not before the mechanism that makes the evidence plausible has been explained.
quests.explanation: The claim states the position. The supporting mechanism explains why fewer hours might not cost productivity, which prepares the reader for the anticipated doubt and its answer, since the evidence only makes sense once the mechanism has set up what to expect from it.
quests.thesisStatement: A four-day work week can maintain the same productivity as a five-day one.

quests.instruction: Assemble a complete, well-built body paragraph using everything from this file: claim, mechanism, evidence, and a closing link that earns its place.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that mandatory cooling-off periods improve major purchase decisions
options: Strong emotions at the point of sale, excitement or urgency, often override the calmer judgment a buyer would apply a day later.
A short mandatory waiting period before a major purchase improves the quality of the decision.
Regions requiring a cooling-off period for large purchases report noticeably lower rates of buyer's remorse and returns.
The waiting period, in effect, gives judgment time to catch up with emotion.
quests.hint: This is the full pattern: a claim, why it should be true, real evidence that it is true, and a sentence that connects the two.
quests.explanation: The claim states the position. The mechanism explains the psychological reason a waiting period would help, which the evidence then supports with real outcomes. The link back closes by naming, in one line, exactly why the mechanism and evidence point to the same conclusion.
quests.thesisStatement: A short mandatory waiting period before a major purchase improves the quality of the decision.

quests.instruction: Build this capstone paragraph so a counterpoint is acknowledged without breaking the paragraph's unity or its logical order.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that limiting class sizes improves teaching quality, while acknowledging its cost
options: A teacher with fewer students can adjust an explanation in real time for the two or three who are visibly confused, something impossible to do reliably in a room of forty.
Where resources allow it, smaller classes remain one of the most direct ways to improve teaching quality.
Reducing class sizes, however, requires hiring more teachers and building more classrooms, a cost many schools cannot absorb quickly.
Smaller class sizes allow teachers to notice and respond to individual students far more effectively.
quests.hint: The cost should be acknowledged only after the benefit has been fully explained, and the refined position should weigh both rather than ignoring either.
quests.explanation: The claim opens with the core benefit. The mechanism explains how that benefit works in practice, which the acknowledged cost then honestly complicates. The refined position closes by weighing the benefit against the cost, rather than pretending the cost does not exist.
quests.thesisStatement: Smaller class sizes improve teaching quality directly, though the cost of achieving them is real.

quests.instruction: Full capstone integration: order a paragraph that moves from claim through mechanism and evidence to a conclusion that resists an obvious oversimplification.
quests.essayTopic: Write a body paragraph arguing that gratitude journaling can improve wellbeing without overstating its power
options: Studies comparing regular journalers with a control group found small but consistent improvements in reported mood over several weeks.
Writing down a few things a person is grateful for each day can modestly improve their overall wellbeing.
The practice works by redirecting attention toward what is already going well, which counteracts a natural tendency to dwell on problems.
The effect is real but modest, which means gratitude journaling works best as one habit among several, not as a substitute for addressing serious difficulties.
quests.hint: The conclusion should reflect the actual size of the evidence, neither dismissing it nor overselling it. Place it only after the evidence has been given honestly.
quests.explanation: The claim states a measured position from the start. The mechanism explains the psychological process, and the evidence supports it with a realistic outcome. The careful conclusion closes by matching the claim's caution, resisting the temptation to overstate what modest evidence actually shows.
quests.thesisStatement: Gratitude journaling can modestly improve wellbeing, working best alongside other habits rather than as a standalone solution.
